thread.title: Dow Jones Giants Apple, Goldman Sachs Team Up On Credit Card: Report

author: MICHAEL LARKIN
title: Dow Jones Giants Apple, Goldman Sachs Team Up On Credit Card: Report

organizations.name: goldman sachs team up on credit card

text:
Dow Jones giants Apple ( AAPL ) and Goldman Sachs ( GS ) reportedly are teaming up to issue a credit card.
X The card will have Apple Pay branding and could launch early next year, sources told the Wall Street Journal it will carry. It's another way for the iPhone giant to extract cash from customers and boost its Apple Pay profile. For Goldman Sachs, which is moving into retail banking, this would be the first time that it's issues a credit card.
Apple and Goldman are working out the terms and benefits of the planned card. In addition, the partnership will see Goldman offer in-Apple Store loans to customers buying iPhones and other products.
An Apple-Goldman card would push aside Barclays ( BCS ) as Apple's rewards-card partner. Apple and U.K.-based Barclays currently offer a credit card with interest-free financing on Apple devices and points toward Apple Store and iTunes gift cards.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple rose 1.4% to 190.04 on the stock market today , hitting a new all-time high and rising for a ninth straight session. The stock is just extended from a 179.04 buy point in a double-bottom base, MarketSmith analysis shows . Goldman rose 0.7%, but hit resistance at its 200-day line. Barclays inched up 0.7%.
Apple is trying to ramp up services revenue as iPhone sales growth slows down. The Apple Pay platform generates revenue on each transaction, however adoption has been slower than executives hoped. Improving use is a key part of its strategy.
Goldman Goes Retail Goldman is seeking to move into consumer banking to offset a slump in its core securities-trading business. Revenue has fallen by more than 60% since the financial crisis, though its once-quiet bond and stock trading desks roared back to life in the first quarter.
Back in 2016 it launched retail banking business Marcus for online savings accounts and personal loans. Last month the company said it had bought the personal finance app Clarity Money, which will strengthen its Marcus online lending service. Management is also looking into adding credit cards and wealth-management tools.
"This move clearly shows that Goldman Sachs sees big opportunity in credit cards," said Matt Schulz, CreditCards.com's senior industry analyst. "Despite worries in the industry about the rising cost of rewards and the uptick in delinquencies, banks still make a ton of profit off of credit cards and Goldman Sachs wants to get its share."
Schulz added: "This isn't just about short-term profits for Goldman Sachs. It's also about branding. It's about tying their brand with Apple's hugely powerful brand and potentially establishing long-term relationships with Apple's highly desirable customer base, who tend to be younger than your typical Goldman client, more affluent than the average American and famously loyal to Apple."
Amazon's Banking Move Amazon ( AMZN ) reportedly has talked with JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) and Capital One Financial ( COF ) to create a checking-account-like product intended to attract teenagers that don't have credit or debit cards.
Amazon's business-lending service also has reportedly partnered with Bank of America ( BAC ) to offer small-business loans.
An account for cardless teenagers would allow Amazon to draw in that population early. It would also give the online sales gaint, already armed with reams of customer data, a greater sense of their purchasing habits.
